careers.title: What do you do in the hair world?
labels: Editorial, commercial, film, or TV work.
Just getting started—or getting back into it.
careers.note: Pick everything that applies. You don’t have to fit in one box.

primary.title: You do more than one thing. Where should we start?
primary.note: Pick one. We can make a separate plan for the others.

goal.title: Thirty days from now, what would make you say, “That was worth it”?
labels: More clients or paid gigs I actually want.
Getting paid more for the work I already do.
Knowing where my money goes—and keeping more of it.
A life that doesn’t revolve around work.
Steadier income. Less holding my breath.
I need help figuring out where to start.
goal.note: Pick one. Your entire life doesn’t need a makeover by Tuesday.

load.title: How’s your book looking?
labels: Starting or rebuilding. Plenty of openings.
I have clients. I could use more.
I need to look at the actual numbers.

owner_load.title: How busy is your salon?
labels: Starting or rebuilding. Plenty of empty chairs.
We have clients. There’s room for more.
I need to check the numbers.

available.title: How much time can you realistically give this each week?

budget.title: What can you spend on bringing in more business this month?
labels: More than $300, if it makes sense.

savings.title: If you couldn’t work, how long would your savings cover the bills?
labels: I need to do the math.

savinghabit.title: Are you putting money aside?
labels: When I can. My income changes.
Yes. I make it a regular thing.
I need to check what I’m actually saving.

color_pay.title: How do you get paid?
labels: I work for myself. The money comes to me—and so do the bills.

color_control.title: Who gets the final say on your prices and appointment times?
labels: The salon and I decide together.

color_signature.title: What kind of color work do you want more of?

color_time.title: Are you finishing on time, or is your next client already waiting?
labels: I’m running behind more often than I’d like.
I haven’t paid attention to it.

color_product.title: Do you know what you spend on color and supplies for each client?
labels: No. I need to figure that out.

color_consult.title: Before you mix the color, what have you and your client agreed on?

color_return.title: Your client’s color looks great. What happens before they leave?
labels: We decide when they need to come back and book it.
I ask if they want to rebook.
The front desk takes it from there.
We say goodbye. The next appointment is anyone’s guess.

cut_pay.title: How do you get paid?
labels: I work for myself. The money comes to me—and so do the bills.

cut_control.title: Who gets the final say on your prices and appointment times?
labels: The salon and I decide together.

cut_specialty.title: What do you want to see more of on your book?
cut_specialty.note: Pick one to focus on this month.

cut_time.title: Do you have enough time booked for each client?
labels: No. I’m rushing to stay on schedule.
More than I need. I could tighten up my day.
Some clients need more time than they’re booked for.

cut_consult.title: Their hair looks great when they leave. Can they do it at home?
labels: Sometimes. Depends on how much we cover.

cut_return.title: Before they leave, what’s the plan for their next appointment?
labels: I tell them when to come back and what to book.
I ask if they want to rebook.
The front desk takes it from there.
I wait for the “Are you free tomorrow?” text.

cut_extras.title: The appointment just got more complicated. Does the price change with it?
labels: Yes. We agree on the extra time and cost first.
No. Apparently, the extra work is my gift to them.
The salon decides what costs extra.
Depends on the day. I need a better answer.

extensions_pay.title: How do you get paid for extension work?
labels: I collect the payment and cover the costs.

extensions_hair.title: Who pays for the hair before you order it?
labels: The client. Before I place the order.

extensions_quote.title: When you quote extensions, what does the client know they’re paying for?
labels: The hair, installation, maintenance, and removal.
We talk it through, but I don’t spell it out in writing.
I need to make that clearer.

extensions_timing.title: Do you know the time and costs for a new install versus maintenance?
labels: No. I lump it all together.

extensions_maintenance.title: Does your extension client leave knowing what maintenance involves?
labels: Yes—and their next appointment is booked.
I’m usually chasing them to come back.
I’m still figuring out how to handle that.

extensions_adjustments.title: When extensions need an unexpected fix, who covers the extra time and cost?
labels: I’m clear about what’s included and what costs extra.

extensions_stock.title: How much unused extension hair do you have sitting around?
labels: Very little. I order for booked clients.
Enough that I should probably know what it’s worth.

session_market.title: What kind of jobs do you want more of?
session_market.note: Pick one to focus on this month.

session_scope.title: Before you say yes to a job, what’s confirmed?
labels: The rate, hours, location, and what I’m expected to do.
Usually just the rate and date.
I say yes. The details show up later.

session_overrun.title: The job runs long. Are you getting paid for the extra time?
labels: Yes. We agreed on that before the job.
I have to bring it up while I’m there.
Usually not. I eat the extra time.
I need to check the terms.

session_expenses.title: Are you paying job expenses out of your own pocket upfront?

session_payment.title: The job’s done. How long until you get paid?
labels: More than 2 weeks, up to a month.
Depends. Chasing payment is apparently part of the job.

session_followup.title: You’ve done a great job. How do you stay on their radar?
labels: I stay in touch with the people I worked with.
I share the work when I have permission.
I wait for the phone to ring.

bridal_team.title: How do you work weddings and events?
labels: I book the jobs and bring a team.
I work on someone else’s team.

bridal_inquiry.title: Where are your wedding and event clients finding you?

bridal_quote.title: What does your quote include?
labels: Services, number of people, travel, timing, and extras.
Mostly the hair. We sort out the rest later.

bridal_trial.title: How do you handle the trial appointment?
labels: The client knows what it costs and what we’ll cover.
It’s included, but I haven’t checked what it costs me.
We figure it out as we go.

bridal_timeline.title: How far in advance do you know the schedule for the wedding or event?
labels: Early enough to plan my day.
I find out when I get there.

bridal_changes.title: They add another person or change the location. What happens?
labels: I confirm the changes and any extra charges in writing.
We talk or text about it, but don’t clearly confirm the new price.
I make it work and absorb the extra time or cost.

bridal_after.title: The event’s over. Do they hear from you again?
labels: Yes. I thank them and ask for a review or referral.
No. I’m on to the next one.

education_buyer.title: Who pays you for your education work?
labels: Stylists who book and pay directly.

education_format.title: What do you want to do more of this month?
labels: Sell a recorded class or resource.
I need to figure that out.

education_outcome.title: What will someone know how to do after taking your class?
labels: Something specific they can use right away.
A few new things, but they may need help putting them into practice.
I need to get clearer on that.

education_prep.title: Are you counting prep and follow-up as work time?
labels: No. Just the time I’m teaching.

education_expenses.title: Who covers travel, models, and supplies when you teach?
labels: We agree on that before I book the job.
It all comes out of my fee.
I usually figure it out afterward.

education_proof.title: They liked the class. Did they actually use anything you taught?
labels: I follow up and ask what’s working.
I ask for feedback, but not what they’ve put into practice.
If they book another class, I take that as a good sign.
Good question. I need to ask.

owner_model.title: What pays the salon’s bills?
labels: A mix of employees and renters.

owner_pay.title: After the salon’s bills are paid, how much is left for you?
labels: Whatever I can transfer without something bouncing.
I need to work that out.

owner_bookings.title: Is the whole salon busy, or just a few people?
labels: Most of the team stays busy.
A few people carry most of the business.
I need to check the numbers.

owner_team.title: What needs the most attention with your team?
labels: Giving clients a consistently good experience.

owner_return.title: Who makes sure clients book their next appointment?
labels: Each stylist does their own thing.
It falls on the front desk.
We need to get clear on that.

owner_stock.title: How do you keep track of products and supplies?
labels: We track what we use and what we have.
We reorder when something runs low.
We have too much sitting around.
I need to see what’s actually there.

owner_delegation.title: What still lands on your plate every day?

manager_pay.title: How do you get paid to manage the salon?
labels: Base pay plus bonuses or commission.
I manage the salon and take my own clients.

manager_authority.title: What can you actually change without asking the owner?
labels: I can make suggestions. The owner decides.
I’m responsible for the results, but don’t have much say.

manager_reports.title: Do you get to see the numbers you’re expected to improve?
labels: We haven’t agreed on what I’m supposed to be improving.

manager_handoff.title: When something needs the owner’s attention, what happens?
labels: We’re clear on what I handle and when they step in.
It usually ends up back on me.

manager_team.title: What makes the day harder than it needs to be?
labels: Not enough people when we need them.
The client experience depends too much on who’s working.
People need more training or help.
Someone thought someone else was handling it.
We’re in a pretty good rhythm.

manager_offduty.title: When you’re off, are you actually off?
labels: Mostly, but I still answer messages.
No. I’m regularly working on my own time.
I’m off the clock, but my head’s still at the salon.

restart_starting.title: Are you starting fresh or starting over?
labels: I’m starting my career in hair.
I’m coming back after a break.
I’ve moved and need to build a clientele.
I’m still working, but I need a fresh start.

restart_setup.title: Do you have a place to take clients?
labels: Yes. Now I need people in the chair.
I’m looking for the right salon.
I’m getting my own space ready.
I’m still figuring that part out.

restart_service.title: What do you want people booking you for first?
labels: That’s what I need help figuring out.

restart_proof.title: If someone asked to see your work, what would you show them?
labels: Recent photos that show what I do best.
Older work. My camera roll needs attention.
A few good examples. I need more.
I need to get some work photographed.

restart_barrier.title: What’s standing between you and taking clients?
labels: My confidence needs to catch up with my skills.

restart_schedule.title: How much can you work without rearranging your entire life?
labels: One regular day or a few set hours each week.
I have room for a full schedule.

other_format.title: What do you actually get paid to do?
labels: Work shoots, events, or other projects.
Teach, create content, or sell products.
A mix. One job title doesn’t cover it.

other_scope.title: Before you start, is everyone clear on the work and the price?
labels: The details sometimes show up after I’ve started.

other_sources.title: Where does your paid work come from?
labels: I reach out and ask for the work.

other_costs.title: After the costs, do you know what you actually made?
labels: No. I know what came in, not what stayed.
I’m paid a wage or salary.

other_repeat.title: Do people hire you again?
labels: Yes, and it’s a steady part of my income.
Yes, but I’d like more of it.
Most of my work is one-off.
This doesn’t apply to my role.

other_time.title: What’s eating up time you’re not getting paid for?
labels: The extras that somehow became part of the job.
Most of my work time is paid.

color_signature: Choose one brunette or dimensional result to show the clients you want to book.
education_prep: Record prep, teaching and follow-up hours for one class.
owner_delegation: Agree which staff questions the team can resolve and which need you.
restart_network: Tell friends and family what you offer and how to book.
restart_barrier: I need to figure out what fits my life.
Choose a reliable work block that fits your current commitments.
other_scope: Too much gets assumed. Not enough gets agreed on.
Confirm the work, price, timing and boundaries in writing before starting.
other_costs: I need a way to figure that out.
Record one job’s pay and costs before making changes.
other_repeat: Start tracking which buyers return before judging repeat demand.

careerstage.title: Where are you in your hair career?
labels: In school. Taking it one mannequin at a time.
Behind the chair and already working.
Beyond the chair, or doing a bit of everything.

studentinterest.title: What kind of work can you see yourself doing?
labels: Ask me after a few more classes.
studentinterest.note: Pick all that apply. You’re allowed to change your mind.

graduation.title: How much school do you have left?
labels: More than 6 months. Still in it.
Good question. My finish date keeps moving.

practice.title: Have you worked on actual people yet?
labels: A few. Building up to it.

direction.title: What’s the plan after graduation?
labels: A salon job where I can keep learning.
Rent a chair or suite and work for myself.
Get through graduation. Then figure it out.

readiness.title: What do you feel least ready for?
labels: Choosing a salon that’s actually right for me.
Talking through the service before I start.
Getting clients to book their next visit.
Understanding what I’ll actually get paid.
Saying no without a ten-minute apology.
readiness.note: Pick what you want help with first.

salonevidence.title: What do you know about the places you’re considering?
labels: I’ve checked the training, pay, costs, and how I’d get clients.
I’ve visited or interviewed, but I still need those answers.
They look good on Instagram. That’s most of my research.

worktype.title: What do you do in the hair world?
labels: I’m trained or licensed, but not taking clients right now.
worktype.note: Pick everything that applies. One job title rarely covers it.

leadershiprole.title: Do you own the salon or manage it?
labels: I manage it. My name isn’t on the lease.

primarywork.title: You do a few things. Which one brings in the most money?

full.title: How full is your book, really?
labels: A few clients. Plenty of openings.

days.title: How many days a week can clients book with you?
days.note: Count the days you offer appointments—even if nobody’s booked yet.

workload.title: Are you getting enough paid work?
labels: About half as much as I’d like.
Almost. I have room for a few more jobs.
Yes. I don’t need to add more.

workdays.title: How many days a week are you working, including the stuff nobody pays you for?
workdays.note: Count prep, travel, supply runs, and admin.

goalpriority.title: We’re not fixing everything by Friday. Where should we start?
goalpriority.note: Choose one of the goals you just selected. The others still count.

paywait.title: The work’s done. How long are you waiting for the money?
labels: More than 2 weeks, up to a month.
More than 1 month, up to 2 months.
More than 2 months, up to 3 months.

workexpenses.title: What comes out of your pocket to do the job?
labels: Tools and replacing what wears out.
Travel, parking, rides, and baggage fees.
Assistants or other people working with me.
Almost nothing. The client or employer covers it.
I need to look. Those little charges add up.

jobsource.title: Where is your paid work actually coming from?
labels: Clients or brands hiring me again.
Brands, producers, planners, or clients reaching out directly.
It’s not coming in consistently yet.
I need to start tracking that.
jobsource.note: Pick all that apply. Bookings, not likes.

outreach.title: What are you doing to get more paid work?
labels: Staying in touch with my agent or rep.
Following up with people who’ve hired me before.
Getting to know the people who hire hair teams.
Reaching out and asking for the job.
Thinking about it. Haven’t done much yet.

repeatwork.title: Once someone hires you, do they hire you again?
labels: I’m new. Too soon to tell.
Most of the people I want to work with hire me again.

repeatfollow.title: The job’s done. Do they hear from you again?
labels: I send a thank-you or follow-up.
I share the work when I have permission.
I stay in touch with the people who hired me.
No. I wait for the next call.

sessionagency.title: Does an agency take a cut of your pay?

sessionfront.title: How often are you covering job expenses before you get paid?
sessionfront.note: Travel, supplies, assistants—the money leaves your account first.

paymodel.title: How do you get paid?
labels: I work for myself. The money comes to me—and so do the bills.
A mix, or I need help sorting it out.

hourlytime.title: Are you working hours that aren’t showing up on your paycheck?
labels: No. My paid hours match my work hours.
Sometimes. Messages, setup, or cleanup happen off the clock.
I need to compare my hours with my pay.

spend.title: What does a client usually spend in your chair?
spend.note: Services only. Leave out tips and take-home products.

returning.title: They came once. Are they coming back?
labels: Too soon to tell. I’m still building.
Some do. Some apparently entered witness protection.

costs.title: After the salon gets its share and your work expenses are paid, what’s left?
labels: I know the number, and it works for me.
I know the number. It needs to be bigger.
That’s what I need help figuring out.

visibility.title: Where are your paying clients finding you?
labels: The salon sends them my way.
New clients aren’t finding me yet.
Good question. I need to start asking.

marketing.title: What have you actually tried to fill your book?
labels: Asking clients, friends, and people I know for referrals.
Meeting people locally and introducing myself.
Not much yet. I need somewhere to start.

network.title: Which of these would you actually do this week?

urgency.title: How soon do you need more clients?
labels: Yesterday. The bills aren’t taking a break.
I need things moving in the next month.
I have some breathing room. I want steady growth.

nextvisit.title: Do you talk about their next visit before they leave?
labels: Yes. What they’ll need and when to come back.
I ask if they want to rebook.
The front desk handles that conversation.
We say goodbye and leave the rest to chance.

followup.title: They left without rebooking. Who makes the next move?
labels: I reach out when they’re due back.
My booking system sends a reminder.
I’m not actually sure anyone follows up.

servicehours.title: Think about the service you book most often. How long does it take, including setup and cleanup?
servicehours.note: Name the service, then enter the total hours and minutes.

workcosts.title: Which work expenses are you paying for?
labels: Card fees, booking apps, and software.
The salon covers my work expenses.
I need to check what’s coming out of my money.

costleak.title: Where do you think you’re losing money?
labels: The salon’s share, rent, or fees.
Discounts, free fixes, and my generous inability to charge for extras.
If I knew, I wouldn’t be asking for help.
costleak.note: Pick one to look at first.

weeklyhours.title: How many hours a week does this career get out of you?
labels: I’ve lost track. That probably says something.
weeklyhours.note: Clients, prep, cleanup, travel, admin. Answering hair messages from bed still counts.

targetdays.title: How many days a week do you actually want to work?
labels: Same days. I’d just like to leave earlier.
Help me figure out what’s realistic.

overrun.title: What keeps you at the salon longer than you want?
labels: Gaps between clients. Still here. Not earning.
My inability to stop squeezing people in.
Messages and paperwork after my last client.
Nothing major. I usually finish on time.
I need to figure out where the day goes.

timeleak.title: Outside the actual job, what takes up the most time?
labels: Prep, shopping, packing my kit, or fittings.
Jobs that run longer than planned.

savings.title: If you couldn’t work, how long would your savings cover the bills?
labels: I need to do the math.
savings.note: Rent, food, and everything else that doesn’t stop charging you.

futurehabit.title: Is money actually making it into savings?
labels: I mean to save. Then somehow I spend what’s left.
When I can. My income changes.
Yes. I put money away regularly.

futurefear.title: What do you want your savings to do for you first?
labels: Get me through a slow month or an emergency.
Let me take time off without panicking.
Support me later in life. I’m not doing hair forever.
Help me move into work that’s easier on my body.
Help me figure out where to start.

workload.title: How’s the salon’s book looking?
workload.note: The whole team—not just your busiest stylist.

jobsource.title: How are paying clients finding the salon?
labels: Google, our website, or contacting us directly.
New clients aren’t coming in consistently.

outreach.title: What are you doing to fill the salon’s book?
labels: Working with outside booking services or partners.
Connecting with local people and businesses.
Promoting specific services or open appointments.
We need to move past hoping the phone rings.

repeatwork.title: Are the salon’s clients coming back?
labels: We’re new. Too soon to tell.

repeatfollow.title: They leave the salon without rebooking. Then what?
labels: We keep showing our work so they remember us.
We check in when they’re due back.
We wait and hope they book.

timeleak.title: What keeps eating up your time at the salon?
labels: Supplies, setup, and getting everything ready.
Waiting around when the schedule falls apart.
Days that never seem to end on time.
I need to see where my time’s going.

workexpenses.title: Which salon expenses are you expected to keep an eye on?
labels: Booking systems, card fees, and software.
We need to get clear on what’s my responsibility.

clients.title: How are you getting people into your chair?
labels: I ask them and book them through school.
I post my work. The part where I tell them how to book needs work.

consultation.title: Before you start, have you talked through more than the inspiration photo?
labels: Yes. The result, time, upkeep, and price.
Some of it. I’m not consistent yet.
I need help knowing what to ask.

rebooking.title: Do you bring up the next appointment, or hope they bring it up?
labels: I tell them when to come back and why.
I ask if they want to rebook. That’s about as far as I get.
I haven’t gotten comfortable asking yet.

money.title: They’ve told you what the job pays. Do you know what that leaves you?
labels: Yes. I’ve checked my costs and what’s still before taxes.
I know the rate or percentage. The rest is a little foggy.
Not yet. I need to see the actual math.

boundaries.title: Someone asks for something you’re not ready to do. What comes out of your mouth?
labels: Sure. Followed by a small internal panic.
I need help saying what I can—and can’t—do yet.

chair: More clients. Those empty appointments aren’t paying rent.
More money without adding another day.
Money that stays in my account long enough to get acquainted.
I love doing hair. It doesn’t need custody of my entire life.
A financial cushion. I’m tired of one surprise bill being an event.
session: More paid jobs on my calendar.
Better pay for the jobs I’m already doing.
Less money disappearing into the cost of doing the job.
Work that leaves room for a life.
Savings for when the phone isn’t ringing.
education: More paid teaching or brand work.
Getting paid properly for the work involved.
Brands and teams bringing me back.
Keeping more after travel, prep, and supplies.
Work that doesn’t take over my entire life.
owner: More clients coming through the door.
More profit without more hours from me.
Knowing where the salon’s money is going.
I own the salon. I’d like it to stop owning me.
A cushion for slow months and surprise bills.
manager: More clients coming through the door.
Pay that matches what I’m responsible for.
A better handle on the numbers I’m expected to improve.
Being off work when I’m off work.
Personal savings so every paycheck isn’t already spoken for.
other: Knowing where the money goes—and keeping more.
A career that leaves room for the rest of my life.
Savings for when things don’t go to plan.

network.past: Ask happy clients to send someone my way.
network.salon: Ask the salon to promote a service I want more bookings for.
network.portfolio: Post a great result and make it easy to book.
network.local: Meet someone locally who could refer clients.
network.models: Book a model for the kind of work I want to show.
network.none: You pick. That’s why I’m here.
